_description:
E-044: the E-036 configuration (xl144 + input noise sigma 0.7 — the best measured stage-2 arm on the monthly ladder) moved onto the PENTAD tensor, over #415's fresh no-longitude-holdout pentad codec, with the stage-2 training pool open to every longitude. Trains a 206.5M stage-2 head (1024x16, K 24, stencil 145, ring spiral:111,4444,0.71,0.5, batch 256, expdecay lr 1e-3 halflife 40k) for 200,000 steps on Z from the frozen f4r2-40M-nolonhold codec. STAGE 1 TRAINS NOTHING: the dispatch resumes !run-415 and states `steps` equal to that checkpoint's OWN recorded step, so train.py's `while s < a.steps` never turns over and the log must print `checkpoint is already at/past --steps; nothing to do`. 

FIVE THINGS A RECIPE CANNOT CARRY, all of which the dispatch must state. (0) `temporal_steps: 200000` — gated by `if: startsWith(inputs.temporal_steps, 'joint:')`, a YAML expression context $RECIPE_TEMPORAL_STEPS cannot reach; tests/test_workflow_config.py case 3 refuses the key and the refusal is correct. (1) `resume: !run-415` — the seed step reads inputs.resume inside an `if:`, same reason. The `!` is load-bearing: #415 publishes NO release asset (codec checkpoints reach model-checkpoints-v1 only by hand — see #386, whose own checkpoint existed on exactly one rented disk for a day), so run-415.pt lives only at /opt/earth-cache/ckpt/run-415.pt on #415's own box and in the expiring `pixelmae-415` artifact. `!` makes a wrong-box dispatch exit in seconds instead of silently training a fresh codec for a day. (2) `steps` — DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and this is the one field that can quietly cost a day. It must equal #415's recorded step, READ OFF THE FILE (ml/CLAUDE.md 0.1), not the 200,000 it was dispatched with: #386 was dispatched at 200,000 and its checkpoint records 166,752, because `max_minutes` re-fits the schedule and train.py assigns the re-fit total back into a.steps. A recipe pinning 200,000 against a 166,752 checkpoint would train 33,248 stage-1 steps, change the codec weights, change the weight hash, and therefore build a DIFFERENT Z under a different cache key — a run that looks perfect and is not the experiment. (3) `runner` — read by runs-on at job start, before any step can set an env var. (4) the window tokens: stencil/ring/seed/sched and everything after `sched:` are parsed out of `window` in scripts/probes_run.sh and are not workflow inputs at all. The exact window string: `recipe:xl144-zn-pentad-nolonhold,stencil:145,ring:spiral:111-4444-0.71-0.5,seed:0,sched:expdecay --lr-cooldown-frac 0 --milestone-steps 600,60000,120000 --input-znoise 0.7`. STENCIL 145, NOT 144: the arm is named for its 144 ring points and the flag counts the centre pixel too. `--input-znoise 0.7` rides in the sched tail because `sched:` goes LAST and probes_run.sh hands everything after it to temporal.py verbatim — E-037's #363/#364 dispatch string, field for field. 

WHY holdout_lon '0,0' IS IN THIS RECIPE EVEN THOUGH STAGE 1 TRAINS NOTHING. train.py ends with save_ckpt(a.steps), which writes `vars(a)` into ml/runs/actions/pixelmae.pt — and that is the file temporal.py then reads for ck['args']['holdout_lon'] to choose the anomaly-transform STATISTICS. Omit this key and train.py's default '-45,-25' is written into the args of a codec that was normalised over every column, so stage 2 z-scores its inputs with a mask the frozen encoder never saw. It would not raise, and it would poison the shared embedding cache: Z is keyed by (codec weight hash, tensor sha256) and neither term can see the transform, so two runs with different statistics share one key. Same value as #415's own recipe, for the same reason it is '0,0' and not 'none': twelve eval scripts under ml/ still float() this field. 

READ-OUTS, per Chris 2026-08-19. HEADLINE: one-step z-space MSE vs persistence (`z_t+1.mse_model` / `mse_persistence`, and the `stage2_val_zmse` curve). SECONDARY, on the CODEC not the head: probe_head + probe_head_raw3x3, which is why `head_probe: true` is pinned here rather than left to a copied input (#416 lost its head number to exactly that, having copied #62's pre-flag inputs). NOT THE HEADLINE, and this is deliberate rather than an oversight: `rapid_probe`, `rapid_probe_kfold` and the in-training `stage2_probe` are all `hid[:, -1].mean(0)` — section-POOLED, the read-out ml/CLAUDE.md section 3 says is distrusted at pentad. They are left emitted because 95 archived bundles carry them and their bit-for-bit reproducibility is the integrity certificate that makes an eval wave readable at all (section 3b, 'protocol determinism'); they are excluded from every claim this run makes. 

CORRIDOR AUC AT PENTAD IS UNBLOCKED as of e9f3d8d (2026-08-20 00:01Z), and the horizon it must use is SETTLED. This paragraph replaces the DO-NOT-DISPATCH-UNTIL note that stood here until 2026-08-20 ~00:10Z; that note's diagnosis was right and its conclusion is now history. WHAT CHANGED. ml/rollout_spatial.py derives its time axis from the tensor (`TimeAxis`, detected by `"bin_index" in d`, step length from `pentad_days` and then CHECKED against the calendar month each label names, for every row) instead of assuming months, and scripts/sroll_run.sh is recipe-driven instead of carrying family-3 literals: $TENSOR drives the tensor, --npz-small is the tensor itself, the Z path is keyed by a codec-weight-hash + data-fingerprint pair computed on the box, and the codec is named by a `ckpt:` token that defaults to the published f3 anchor ONLY on family 3 and REFUSES on any other tensor. All four monthly assumptions this description used to list are gone: month_index -> row_of_label/starts_for_year, ym_to_r -> r_of_row on the axis row, long_roll advances ONE axis row per step with the season token read off that row's TRUE date (the serious one -- it corrupted the model's own input), and band keys carry their day spans. tests/test_roll_monthly_identity.py runs the real evaluator twice on one synthetic ocean, at e9f3d8d and at 9066341, and demands the two roll JSONs be identical, so nothing monthly moved. THE GATE AT PENTAD IS A RECORDED SKIP, NOT A PASS, AND NOT --no-gate. GATE_REF became a per-cadence registry, GATE_REF_BY_CADENCE = {"monthly": GATE_REF}. e017_u1_s0's 0.643 was measured by ml/rollout.py over the MONTHLY family-3 axis (#217) and cannot certify a roll whose steps are a different length, whose starts are a different count and whose bands span different durations. At a cadence with no entry the roll writes gate {pass: null, skipped: true, certified: false, cadence: "pentad", reason: <why, in full>} and warns; sroll_run.sh's final assertion REQUIRES exactly that shape and still requires a PASS at monthly. So the first pentad corridor AUC is UNCERTIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION -- there is nothing for it to be certified against -- and the first PUBLISHED pentad roll is what would ESTABLISH a reference, by registering its own gate head's numbers in GATE_REF_BY_CADENCE. Write every pentad roll number as a first reading until then. THE HORIZON DECISION (Chris, 2026-08-20 ~00:10Z): THE PENTAD ROLL IS HORIZON-MATCHED IN DAYS TO THE MONTHLY ARCHIVE (~365 d), because the question E-044 exists to answer is whether the pentad embedding forecasts BETTER than the monthly one, and a 60-day number has no baseline to be better than. e9f3d8d made the roll PRINT its horizon in days; it does not rescale. ARITHMETIC, all from rollout_spatial.py at e9f3d8d: pentad step_days 5.0, steps_per_year 365.2425/5 = 73.0485, steps_for_months(12) = 73, span_days(73) = 365.0 d against the monthly archive's 12 x 30.436875 = 365.2 d -- 0.2 d apart, and no closer integer exists. The default --horizon 12 at pentad scores 60.0 d. SO: --horizon 73. STARTS ARE THE FREE PARAMETER. starts_for_year returns the last row before Y plus every row inside Y but its last: 12 at monthly, 73 at pentad (the tensor is 3,142 five-day bins from EPOCH 1982-01-01, 43 years, 73 bins/year; holdout years 2009/2017/2023 all have 73). The roll breaks a start when ax.year[s+h] != Y, so monthly costs 12+11+...+1 = 78 scored steps per holdout year = 234 for three (confirmed against probes-417.json's chan_skill n, which falls as 3 x (13-h), and run-417.jsonl's live total 714 = 234 scored + 240 hindcast + 240 future). At --horizon 73 the pentad scored-step count for three holdout years is 219 at 1 start/yr (0.94x monthly), 330 at 2 (1.41x), 441 at 3 (1.88x), 1,440 at 12 (6.15x) and 8,103 at all 73 (34.6x). THE COST FLOOR IS NOT THE STARTS. --long-months/--future-months default to round(20 x steps_per_year) = 1,461 each at pentad against 240 at monthly -- 2,922 steps vs 480, 6.09x, independent of horizon and starts. At the measured monthly rate of 15.06 s/step (714 steps/head; #394 10,750.9 s, #401 10,514.2 s, #413 11,019.0 s, #417 11,082.9 s -- 14.7-15.5 s/step, and a stencil-145 head is only 2% cheaper than a stencil-234 one, so the stencil is NOT the cost driver): --horizon 73 with 3 starts = 3,363 steps = 4.71x monthly = ~14.1 h/head ~ $3.9; with 2 starts 3,252 = 13.6 h; with 12 starts 4,362 = 18.2 h; with all 73 starts 11,025 = 46.1 h. TODAY'S DEFAULT (--horizon 12, 73 starts) is 5,352 steps = 22.4 h/head for a 60-day number. VERDICT: CHRIS'S CHOICE SURVIVES AND IS CHEAPER THAN THE STATUS QUO -- horizon-matched at 3 starts costs 37% LESS than the default and answers the question the default cannot. What it does NOT buy is cost parity with the monthly roll: the 2,922 long+future steps are already 4.09x a whole monthly head before one staggered start, and strict step parity would need long+future <= 495 steps = ~2.5 years of hindcast each, which is exactly the silently-truncated roll e9f3d8d was written to make impossible. A pentad roll costs 4.5-6x a monthly one and the horizon decision is responsible for none of it. RECOMMENDED: --horizon 73 --starts-per-year 3 (stride 24 pentads, phases ~1 Jan / 1 May / 1 Sep) --long-months 1461 --future-months 1461. Three starts is the smallest count giving more than ONE seasonal phase; at 1 start lead time is confounded with season. Say in the harvest that at S starts there are 3S (start, year) samples behind each lead against monthly's 36, so pentad and monthly CIs are NOT like-for-like below S = 12 even though the point estimates are. BANDS AND THE AUC ITSELF. BANDS (rollout_spatial.py:86) is a module constant over h1..12 and band_key only RENAMES it, so at --horizon 73 the three bands cover the first 60 of 365 days and 61 of 73 horizons contribute to no band at all; monthly h1-3 is 30-91 d while pentad h1-3_5-15d is 5-15 d. Define the bands by DAY EDGES -- (0, 91.31], (91.31, 182.62], (182.62, 365.24] d -- which returns h 1-3 / 4-6 / 7-12 EXACTLY at monthly (so test_roll_monthly_identity stays green) and h 1-18 (5-90 d) / 19-36 (95-180 d) / 37-73 (185-365 d) at pentad. Separately and more dangerously, horizon_auc is the UNWEIGHTED mean of msss_clim over h = 1..H: at monthly it averages 12 leads spanning 30-365 d, at pentad H=73 it averages 73 leads spanning 5-365 d, most of them short where skill is highest, so a raw pentad horizon_auc would beat the monthly one on lead-time sampling ALONE. The comparable quantity is the mean over the 12 monthly-equivalent leads, pentad steps {6,12,18,24,30,37,43,49,55,61,67,73} = 30/60/90/120/150/185/215/245/275/305/335/365 d, within 2.4 d of the monthly leads everywhere. That costs NOTHING and needs NO code change -- all 73 chan_skill rows are archived, so it is computed at harvest from the file. Report it as horizon_auc_daymatched and compare only IT against the monthly archive. WHAT THE DECISION STILL NEEDS IN CODE, none of it done in the session that wrote this (ml/rollout_spatial.py and scripts/sroll_run.sh were out of scope): (1) sroll_run.sh:199-201 does not pass --horizon at all, so it falls to argparse's literal 12 = 60 d at pentad -- either pass it from a window token or make the default ax.steps_for_months(12); (2) there is no starts knob, starts_for_year returns every row, and a --starts-per-year stride must leave monthly's list and ORDER untouched or test_roll_monthly_identity fails; (3) BANDS must become day-defined; (4) --long-months/--future-months are not passed either, but their defaults are already cadence-correct; (5) job_timeout -- #417's monthly sroll ran three heads in 700 min, one pentad head needs >= 1,000 min and a seed pair >= 1,900 min. UNVERIFIED and the largest uncertainty above: every hour quoted is the MONTHLY per-step rate. Nothing has ever rolled the pentad tensor. P is 86,698 vs 84,405 (1.027x), C 40 vs 39 (1.026x), d_z 32 vs 64 (halves the Z gather and the decoder input projection), head 206.5M vs 217.3M (0.95x); expected to net within +/-15%, but that is arithmetic. The first sroll progress record settles it in minutes -- read it before letting a 14-hour job run. NONE OF THIS BLOCKS THIS RECIPE: temporal.py does not call rollout_spatial, the head this run trains is a real artefact, and the one-step MSE it reports is sound. Corridor AUC comes from a SEPARATE sroll: dispatch over the head this run publishes, which needs #415's codec published by name (sroll_run.sh refuses to guess off family 3), the pentad tensor warm plus its _X.npy sidecar or a ~34 GB extraction, and the same 16.24 GiB Z. Full spec: claude/E044-pentad-stage2-spec.md sections 7a and 7b. 

UNMEASURED AT PENTAD, every one of them (section 3b: 'anything at pentad or daily cadence — none; every arm at the new cadences is n = 1'). (i) The EMBED PASS has never been run over the full pentad window by anything: every pentad probe so far (#390/#392/#397/#406/#409) embedded the ~265-pixel RAPID section only, which is where the '2.5 minutes' figure in E-038 comes from — it is NOT a full-window number and must not be scaled. The only full-window measurement in the archive is 95 minutes for 516 x 84,405 = 43.55M pixel-encodes through the 40.7M patch-3 anchor (E-008, #119/#120). Pentad is 3,142 x 86,698 = 272.4M pixel-encodes, 6.26x, through a codec whose transformer body is ~0.95x the cost (12 x 512^2 vs 10 x 576^2) over 40 channel tokens instead of 39: ESTIMATE ~9-10 HOURS, arithmetic not measurement. (ii) Z is 3,142 x 86,698 x 32 x 2 B = 17.43 GB = 16.24 GiB — 3.1x the monthly 5.2 GiB, not 6.1x, because this codec's d_z is 32 where the anchor's is 64. That is 11 chunks at embed_cache_sync's 1.5 GiB, well inside its 64-chunk pull loop. (iii) The per-step cost should be FLAT or slightly lower than monthly's 0.27 s/step: the window is K x stencil x d_z regardless of cadence and d_z halves, so the gather is 114 MB/step against 228 MB and the input projection is 145x32+2 instead of 145x64+2 — hence 206.5M head params, not the monthly arm's 211.4M. Nothing in the window machinery scales with T. (iv) What DOES scale with T is the in-training transport probe, which loops `for t_ in range(K-1, T)` once per probe: 3,119 forwards instead of 493, ten probes plus the final eval-3 pass, ~2.5 h of the job — spent entirely on the pooled number this run does not report. (v) MEMORY. temporal.py keeps the tensor eager: np.nan_to_num(X) copies 34 GB beside the 34 GB X and np.isfinite(X) adds a 17 GB bool, an ~85 GB peak before `del X`, then ~51 GB steady, plus ~4.0 GB of int64 pool indices (251M windows with the block returned) and the 17.4 GB Z in page cache. 126 GB BOXES ONLY, and the peak is close enough to matter — probe_kfold.py has had the LazyPixels treatment for this since #388 and temporal.py has NOT. 

SEEDS. Section 3b's one-seed licence does not reach here: it is granted only for rolled corridor AUC at the xl tier on the frozen f3 anchor and the monthly tensor, and this run changes the codec, the tensor and the cadence at once. 'The first result at a tier buys its own replication.' Dispatch seed 0 first; a seed-1 arm is required before any number here is a level rather than a first reading.

2026-08-21 · WHAT #423 MEASURED, AND THE ONE FIELD THE RE-DISPATCH CHANGES. #423 ran this recipe and DIVERGED: best val/persistence 0.540 at step 2,000, then grad norm 8.24 -> 787 -> 3,891 -> 13,052 with two excursions to zmse 121 / val 227, cancelled at step 28,000 after 2.9 h of training. The diagnosis, from artefacts. (1) THE Z-SCALE DIFFERENCE IS REAL AND REPLICATED, and it is NOT a d_z artefact: `stage2_monitor.val_persistence` is `.pow(2).mean()` (temporal.py:1814), a PER-COMPONENT mean, so d_z 32 vs 64 and C 40 vs 39 do not enter it. This codec's z-space has RMS one-step change sqrt(21.44622) = 4.631 against the monthly anchor's sqrt(3.09512) = 1.759 — 2.63x — and the codecs' own stage-1 probes agree independently and in pairs: `z_mse_persistence` finishes at 19.875 (#415) and 20.98 (#386) on pentad against 2.953 (#62) and 3.298 (#63) on monthly. (2) BUT THE SCALE IS NOT THE DESTABILISER. AdamW is invariant to a global gradient rescale — measured, not asserted: multiplying the loss by 6.929 (the exact val_persistence ratio) moves a 400-step AdamW trajectory by 1.3e-4 relative. So `stage2_grad_norm` reading 8.24 at pentad where the monthly arm reads 1.24 is a UNITS statement about the z-space, not evidence of pathology, and a lower LR is NOT indicated: the same lr 1e-3 is healthy at monthly and was healthy at pentad for 4,000 steps. (3) THE DESTABILISER IS THE MISSING CLIP. Until 2026-08-21 `grep -n 'clip_grad\|max_norm\|grad_clip' ml/temporal.py` returned NOTHING, and one unclipped step at 13,051.8 = 1,582x the healthy 8.25 grows AdamW's second moment by 2,503x, so sqrt(v) rises 50x and every honest gradient for the next ~1/(1-beta2) = 1,000 steps is divided by 50. That is the shape #423 shows, and after step 6,000 its norm never returns below 1,000 — a sustained regime change, not isolated spikes. (4) `--input-znoise 0.7` IS MIS-SCALED, AND IN THE BENIGN DIRECTION. The flag is an ABSOLUTE sigma; E-036/E-037 sized 0.7 on the MONTHLY z-space, where it is 0.398 x sqrt(val_persistence). On this codec's z-space the same 0.7 is 0.151 x — 2.63x WEAKER than the perturbation that was measured. It is therefore not the divergence (weaker noise does not explode gradients) and it is also NOT the intervention E-036/E-037 measured, only the same number; every claim off this arm must say so. temporal.py now prints and records both ratios (`stage2_monitor.z_rms`, `input_znoise_rel_pers`, `input_znoise_rel_zrms`) so no future run has to derive its own z-scale indirectly. THE RE-DISPATCH THEREFORE CHANGES EXACTLY ONE FIELD: `--grad-clip 128` appended to the window's `sched:` tail. 128.0 is 3.231x the LARGEST grad norm in the entire monthly archive (8,080 logged norms over 83 runs, every one at val_persistence 3.09512: median 0.566, p99 4.279, p99.9 14.448, max 39.6165 on #308), so 0 of 8,080 would have been clipped; it is 15.5x the healthy pentad norm, so it does not bind a healthy pentad run either; it is 6.15x below the smallest pentad excursion; and it turns the worst observed step's second-moment damage from 50x into 1.11x. `--grad-clip` DEFAULTS TO 0 = OFF and OFF MAKES NO CALL AT ALL, so every archived monthly number stays bit-reproducible; tests/test_e044_grad_clip.py proves it against the pinned pre-fix revision 877ae5b, and proves separately that a clip at a threshold nothing reaches is bit-identical too. LR, warmup, seed, znoise and every architecture field are UNCHANGED, so the re-dispatch is a one-variable test against #423's own trace.
_provenance: Stage-2 geometry copied field-for-field from ml/recipes/xl144-nolonhold.json, which took it from the PUBLISHED ARTEFACT e032xlx600_u1_s0__temporal.pt (range-read from model-checkpoints-v1 on 2026-08-19: K 24, steps 200000, batch 256, lr 1e-3, d_model 1024, layers 16, lr_schedule expdecay, lr_halflife 40000, lr_cooldown_frac 0.0, lr_warmup 2000, ring_km 'spiral:111,4444,0.71,0.5', stencil 145, unroll 1, milestone_steps '600,60000,120000'). The znoise value is E-036/E-037's: --input-znoise 0.7, set from the model's own measured one-step error (sqrt(val_zmse) ~ 0.74) and never tuned, and it is the largest replicated stage-2 effect in the log — +0.045 / +0.050 corridor AUC across two pairs against a tier spread of 0.0021. Its dispatch form is E-037 #363/#364's window tail verbatim. The CODEC fields are ml/recipes/f4r2-40M-nolonhold.json's, i.e. what #415 (E-043e fresh 38.0M pentad r2 codec, all longitude columns) is training right now: family4_na025_pentad_r2, d_z 32, patch 1, 512x12, 4 heads, d_dec 256, holdout_lon '0,0'. head_probe true is ml/CLAUDE.md section 3's standing requirement at the new cadences. batch 512 is the stage-1 field and is inert here (nothing trains); stage 2 takes temporal.py's own default of 256, and probes_run.sh hard-codes --K 24, so neither is settable from a dispatch. Head parameter count 206,535,712, computed by instantiating TemporalTransformer(d_z=32, d_model=1024, n_heads=4, n_layers=16, k_max=24, stencil=145) — the same construction returns 211,352,640 at d_z 64, which is E-032's own '211.4M' and is how the count was checked. Pentad ocean pixel count 86,698 and T 3,142 are build_family4.py's measured inventory as recorded in E-038a's scale table, not family 3's 84,405. NOTHING HAS BEEN RUN AT THIS CONFIGURATION, AT THIS CADENCE, OR ON THIS CODEC. This recipe is the dispatch surface; every number in its _description marked ESTIMATE is arithmetic over one monthly measurement and becomes a measurement when the run lands. Dispatch spec: claude/E044-pentad-stage2-spec.md.
